body.en: AP Calculus BC Free-Response Questions (FRQs) covers essential College Board AP Calculus BC competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Multi-Part FRQ Layout & Point Allocation

body.en: Master the structure of standard BC FRQs: Part A (Calculator active, Questions 1-2) and Part B (No calculator, Questions 3-6). Points are partitioned into setup, derivative/integral, and contextual answer.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

On Question 1 of Section II, water flows into a tank at rate \(R(t)\) and leaves at rate \(L(t)\). Write the integral representing the net change in water volume from \(t = 0\) to \(t = 6\).

solution.en: The net rate of change is \(R(t) - L(t)\). By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: \[ \text{Net Change} = \mathbf{\int_0^6 (R(t) - L(t))\,dt}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Polar & Parametric Velocity / Acceleration FRQ Scenarios

body.en: Evaluate velocity vectors, speed, total distance, and polar tangents under strict College Board justification criteria.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

A particle moves in the xy-plane with velocity \(\vec{v}(t) = \langle 2t, \cos(\pi t) \rangle\). At \(t = 1\), is the particle moving to the right or left, and is it moving up or down? Justify.

solution.en: At \(t = 1\): \(x'(1) = 2(1) = 2 > 0\), so the particle is moving to the right. \(y'(1) = \cos(\pi) = -1 < 0\), so the particle is moving down.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Comprehensive Question 6 Taylor Series FRQ Protocol

body.en: Deconstruct past Question 6 FRQs: finding general terms, radius of convergence, differentiating/integrating term-by-term, and applying alternating series or Lagrange error bounds.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

A function \(f\) has Maclaurin series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^{n+1} x^n}{n \cdot 2^n}\). Write the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin series for \(f'(x)\).

solution.en: The first three terms of \(f(x)\) are: \[ f(x) = \frac{x}{2} - \frac{x^2}{8} + \frac{x^3}{24} - \cdots \] Differentiating term-by-term with respect to \(x\): \[ f'(x) = \mathbf{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{x}{4} + \frac{x^2}{8} - \cdots} \]
